In what ways? Pop fashion in the style of some decade -- be it long collars, pastel shirts, or baggy pants -- were largely constructions of limited clothing choices and cultural icons. Today, clothing choices have exploded, allowing retro, niche, and over-the-top to all blend into a cosmopolitan nostalgia of functionality and subculture. Similarly, language has been slowly homogenizing since the invention of the radio, and the rise of el rando on Youtube has opened that up to everybody everywhere.

Once manufacturing and computing get cheap enough, then restricted media channels have much less importance, and people go back to forming their own subcultures. That means they can be weirder than John Travolta's disco suit, but at the same time have a weaker hold on culture because of its niche status. So the default acceptable cosmopolitan style gets stronger, even as its subcultures pull on it through the Overton window to normalize perversions and ugly things.
